# Uncommon Sense

> Uncommon Sense Consulting Limited is the consultancy of Martin Jackson, a fractional CTO and board adviser based in Watford, UK. He helps founders, boards and makers with strategy, technology and AI decisions that hold up under scrutiny.

## Services

- Fractional CTO: senior technical leadership a few days a month. Architecture, hiring, delivery and the decisions a team is waiting on.
- Board advisory: an independent technical voice on the board. Plain-English reads on technology risk, spend and plans.
- AI governance and assurance: evidence gates before an AI feature ships. What it must prove, who signs it off, and what happens when it drifts.

## Who it is for

- Founders who are the bottleneck on technical decisions.
- Boards asked to approve technology and AI plans they cannot easily test.
- Makers, charities and small teams who need practical, budget-sized technology advice.

## Writing

<!-- writing:start -->
- [Bread crumbing](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/bread-crumbing/): "Explain it to me as if I was a cocker spaniel." I sometimes say that. It usually comes after the fourth or fifth message. I ask a question.
- [Rent forever](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/rent-forever/): A while back I wanted to run an Oracle database on a VMware cluster. The point of the cluster was simple.
- [The clones that had an answer key](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/artcraft-answer-key/): The story going round is that someone vibe coded Photoshop.
- [When the picture looked right](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/when-the-picture-looked-right/): "Stop." I said it to the AI assistant I was using to design a card for a maker's stall.
- [The log that cannot be edited afterwards](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/log-that-cannot-be-edited/): When AI writes code no human will read, review stops being a control. What survives is evidence of behaviour. I posted that three weeks ago.
- [It's very expensive](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/its-very-expensive/): "It's very expensive." That is what the stallholder said to me, before I had even mentioned the price. I had picked up a crochet belt on their stall.
- [The bottleneck moved](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/bottleneck-moved/): I've discovered an unexpected productivity problem in 2026. I'm increasingly waiting for AI to finish its work.
- [When someone refused my first answer](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/refuse-the-first-answer/): "If you were 28 like me, with what you know now, what would you be doing?" Orji Matthew asked me that in a LinkedIn message this week, from Abuja.
- [The decision problem](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/decision-problem/): Most engineering organisations I see don't have a delivery problem. They have a decision problem.
- [Judgement over execution](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/judgement-over-execution/): Dropping my own recommendation was the best decision I made for a client this summer. My diagnosis was correct. One person's hours limited their output.
- [The AI Act deadline that did not snooze](https://uncommonsense-uk.com/writing/ai-act-snooze/): Nearly four weeks ago, parts of the EU AI Act still became applicable. The high-risk deadlines moved. Others did not.
